question: The task is the same (MCI vs healthy controls in older adults), but the measurement channel is not. P-114 (Seifallahi et al., pack pdf/P-115.txt) uses Kinect gait (the gait/motor channel). P-58 uses ASR-derived temporal parameters of spontaneous speech (the speech/language channel).
metric: Accuracy with accuracy, once P-58's accuracies are read from its tables. The ledger's '67-92% range' mixes accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and F1 across feature subsets, so it is not an accuracy estimate (a misreading covered by condition 6); the printed accuracies are judged instead.

figures.P-114: Accuracy 93% (n = 150: 70 MCI, 80 HC; ANFIS protocol not stated), Wilson 95% CI 0.878-0.961.
figures.P-58: Speaker-wise nested leave-one-out CV, n = 33 per language. English, all 15 parameters: accuracy 84.8% = 28/33, Wilson 0.691-0.934 (contains 93%). Hungarian, all parameters: 75.8% = 25/33, Wilson 0.590-0.872 (excludes 93%; 75.8% is also outside P-114's CI). Best subset (filler-related, Hungarian): 90.9% = 30/33, Wilson 0.764-0.969 (contains 93%).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure is possible across channels: neither paper reports a result in the other's channel or cohort.
reason: The measurement channels differ (Kinect gait vs speech tempo and pause parameters), so the pair fails condition 1 whatever the numbers. Only P-58's Hungarian all-feature accuracy (75.8%) lies beyond uncertainty from P-114's 93%. Its English and best-subset accuracies do not.

quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
The MCI subjects of the present study were selected through clients of the Iran dementia and Alzheimer’s Association (IDAA) in Tehran city of Iran
we got quite similar scores (67-92%) as we did in the monolingual cases (67-92% as well).
Both the English-speaking (n = 33; New York, NY, USA) and the Hungarian-speaking (n = 33; Szeged, Hungary) participants were diagnosed as MCI or HC.
Besides an accuracy score of 84.8%, the recall/sensitivity and specificity values were also around 85%.
classifying one further MCI subject correctly leads to an increase of about 7%.
